name: Libyan Sharba Libiya
description: Sharba Libiya, Libya's national soup and the centerpiece of every Ramadan table, is genuinely heavily spiced - real recipes describe it as a dish where 'more truly is more' with the spice blend (bzar/hararat), not a place to hold back. Fresh dried mint rubbed between the palms directly into the pot right at the end is a real, essential finishing touch, not a garnish.

ingredients_full.note: a full, heaping teaspoon - don't hold back, real versions are heavily spiced

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Brown the lamb with the onion, 6-7 minutes.

Add the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes, turmeric, pepper, paprika, cinnamon, cardamom, and cloves - be genuinely generous with the spices here, real sharba is boldly seasoned, not lightly touched.
Add the chickpeas and 3 cups water, and simmer 30-35 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the pasta and simmer 12-15 minutes until tender.
Turn off the heat and rub the dried mint between your palms directly into the pot - this real finishing step is what defines sharba's aroma.

name: Libyan Bazin
description: Bazin, a dense, unleavened dough mound served with a spiced meat sauce, is Libya's most traditional communal dish, real technique kneading the dough hard and long to build its dense, real elastic texture.
steps_detailed: Knead the flour, salt, and water into a very stiff, dense dough, working it hard for several minutes until smooth.
Steam or boil the dough ball until firm all the way through, 25-30 minutes.
Brown the beef, then add the tomatoes, turmeric, and cumin, being generous with both spices, and simmer 20-22 minutes.
Shape the bazin dough into a mound and serve the sauce poured over and around it.

name: Libyan Couscous
description: Libyan couscous, real technique steaming the grains two or three times with fluffing between each round, is a beloved dish especially for Friday family lunches, real spicing here bold rather than restrained.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Chickpeas (garbanzo beans, bengal gram), mature seeds, canned, drained solids

steps_detailed: Simmer the chicken, carrot, chickpeas, cumin, and turmeric in 1.5 cups water 25-28 minutes until the chicken is tender - be generous with both spices.
Toss the dry couscous with a little oil and water.
Steam over the simmering stew 10 minutes, then fluff and steam again 8-10 minutes for properly light, separate grains.
Serve the stew and broth over the finished couscous.

name: Libyan Hararat Spice Blend
description: Hararat (also called bzar), Libya's essential all-purpose spice blend, is genuinely built from equal parts of several warming spices together - real Libyan cooks use this generously throughout their cooking, not sparingly.
steps_detailed: Toast each spice briefly in a dry pan, 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Mix together in roughly equal parts and store in an airtight container - this is a bold blend meant to be used generously.

name: Libyan M'battan
description: M'battan, a genuine Ramadan specialty, is real potato wedges cut into pockets, stuffed with spiced minced meat, then battered and deep-fried - not a layered casserole, which was wrong here before. Real technique cooks the meat filling until it dries out and releases its own fat, which is what makes the mince stick together well enough to hold inside the potato pocket.

ingredients_full.note: cut into thick wedges, each sliced most of the way through to form a pocket
tbsp, chopped, standing in for parsley

ingredients.note: cut into thick wedges, each sliced most of the way through to form a pocket
tbsp, chopped, standing in for parsley

steps_detailed: Cook the onion in a little oil until fragrant, then add the beef, ginger, cinnamon, and black pepper, being generous with both spices.
Cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the meat dries out and releases its own fat, 10-12 minutes - this real drying-out is what makes the mince cohesive enough to stuff.
Stir in the cilantro and let cool slightly.
Stuff the meat mixture firmly into each potato pocket.
Whisk the flour and egg with a splash of water into a smooth batter, and coat each stuffed potato wedge.
Deep-fry, turning, 6-8 minutes, until the potato is cooked through and the coating is deeply golden and crisp.

description: Brik, a crispy fried pastry with a soft egg center, shared with neighboring Tunisia, a beloved Libyan snack especially during Ramadan.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids

ingredients.ingredient: Fish, tuna, light, canned in water, drained solids

steps_detailed: Spoon the tuna onto a phyllo sheet, make a well, and crack the egg into it.

name: Libyan Grilled Lamb
description: Grilled lamb seasoned with real hararat (the full seven-spice blend), not a generic cumin rub, is a beloved Libyan dish for gatherings - real hararat includes black pepper, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, coriander, and cumin together, and some home cooks add caraway seed for a sharper, nuttier edge.
steps_detailed: Mix the lamb with the cumin, cinnamon, cloves, nutmeg, coriander, black pepper, and garlic, being genuinely generous with all the spices - this real, full hararat blend is what distinguishes Libyan lamb from a simple cumin rub.
Grill or pan-sear, 4-5 minutes per side, until well charred and cooked through.
